limits: trust boundary: every rule holds only against a caller that reaches the store through the engine; a process that can write the store folder can append records itself, and one that can start its own engine on it can ignore every check

in this demo the agent, the store folder and the human cosign key belong to one OS user: it shows the cosign mechanism, not the separation that "the agent cannot self-cosign" needs (key outside the agent's reach AND no agent write access to the store folder or way to run another engine on it)
the opener of a key is trusted for its tenant, original and facts; disasters 2 and 3 are blocked relative to those values; the tenant field is not authenticated
the read airlock checks only the top-level tenant_id of the rows passed to it and returns parsed copies of the checked bytes
a lease is bound to (request id, tenant, key); only handlers that opened a lease are covered

pins: the engine pins the refund binary and (through its compiled-in helper) the checker model; the store pins the SHA-256 of the Node binary at init (inventory only); a cosign is verified by /usr/bin/ssh-keygen, which the engine checks (root-owned, not writable by group or other, no symbolic link on its path) but does not pin: the system OpenSSH is a trusted assumption; the helper files are checked at every run but still run by path: the engine uid or root can change them between check and run
Stripe and PayPal are LOCAL FAKE in-process stand-ins; SIGKILL is not a power loss; end_to_end=false

not_killed.why: the binding of the second open (ssh-keygen opens the key file again by path) to the checked descriptor. Not observable in a repeatable way: it needs the key file to be replaced between the two opens (a race); no case claims it

robustness.H01, H06: the demo race and the fuzz burst without the compare-and-swap: the lock serializes the 50 requests, so the result does not depend on which process wins
robustness.M03_compare_and_swap: case race: with the lock kept, the second request sees the first commit (TOTAL_CAP, not STALE); no timing
robustness.M25_no_lock and S17_shared_lock: case lock: one holder parked at kill point a with the lock; two waiters must not answer within 5 s; after the kill exactly one commits. Two independent signals.
robustness.S16_lock_after_wal_read: case trace: the first store-file event must be the exclusive flock (no timing)

trusted_assumptions: macOS kernel and drive: fcntl(F_FULLFSYNC) returns 0 only after the drive was asked to store the data; flock is exclusive and is released at process end; APFS keeps what F_FULLFSYNC reported. NOT tested at power loss.

rustc 1.92.0, LLVM and the Rust standard library; Node 24.3.0 (the booking checker only; no Node runs for a cosign); the Dafny 4.11.0 compiler and JavaScript runtime; bignumber.js 9.3.1 loaded from the pinned node_modules (package-lock.json; checked by scripts/javascript_env.py, and by its own SHA-256 pin in booking_check.cjs since review D2); Python 3.10.11.

The system OpenSSH is a trusted assumption: /usr/bin/ssh-keygen (OpenSSH_10.3p1 with LibreSSL 3.3.6 on the measured machine) verifies every cosign signature (Ed25519). It is checked (owner uid 0, no group or other write bit, no symbolic link on its path) but NOT pinned: an OS update can change it without a change of any store. OpenSSH with LibreSSL is now in the trusted base for cosign in place of Node/V8: smaller and widely reviewed, but not zero. Its answers are mapped strictly: only two exact results count, anything else is HELPER_FAILED.
The JSON-to-Dafny generator of diff_policy.py (owner decision, Goal 20 plan line 8).

Trust boundary (review finding 1): every rule holds only against a caller that reaches the store THROUGH the engine. A process that can write the store folder can append records itself, and one that can start its own engine build on the store can ignore every check. "The agent cannot self-cosign" needs the private key out of the agent's reach AND no agent write access to the store folder and no way for the agent to run another engine on it. In the demo all three belong to one OS user: it shows the mechanism only.
The opener of a key is trusted (review finding 6): the money caps rest on the original amount and the facts that the opener chooses; the tenant field is not authenticated.
The read airlock checks only the TOP-LEVEL tenant_id of the rows passed to it (review finding 10); a nested row of another tenant passes. It sees only the rows passed to it.

What pins what: the engine embeds the Node booking helper (include_str!, no helper file is read at run time) and pins the refund binary (SHA-256 b8ed5ec2...7bb8); the store pins the SHA-256 of the Node binary in its genesis record at init (inventory only); booking_check.cjs pins the compiled model (e705ec49...85f4); the genesis record pins the policy files (FNV-1a-128, not cryptographic) and the cosign key; bin/forge-airlock re-checks its private refund copy; booking_check.cjs pins bignumber.js 9.3.1 (SHA-256 08ff132b...f0ce, review D2); nothing pins the engine binary itself or /usr/bin/ssh-keygen. Review D2: at every run the refund binary and Node pass an ownership walk (owner root or the engine uid, no group or other write bit up to /) and are checked (the refund binary hashed, Node re-hashed when its identity changed); they are still run by path (no fexecve on macOS; exec of /dev/fd/N gave EACCES), so root or the engine uid can change a file between the check and the exec; in the one-user flow that closes nothing against the caller. The checks cover the helper FILE only, not the libraries it loads: the Homebrew Node loads 9 libraries from /opt/homebrew/opt (group admin may write them), so any admin-group user can still run code in the booking checker (open, owner decision). macOS ACLs are not read. The test seams AIRLOCK_TEST_HELPERS, AIRLOCK_TEST_UNPINNED_BINARY, AIRLOCK_TEST_SSH_KEYGEN and AIRLOCK_TEST_UNTRUSTED_SSH_KEYGEN exist only in the kill_points build.

Cosign: an agent that runs as the same OS user as the key owner can read a 0600 key file; "the agent cannot self-cosign" holds only when the private key is outside its reach (and see the trust boundary above). Weak (small-order or non-canonical) Ed25519 keys and signature R values, and S >= L, are refused natively.

FNV-1a-128 collisions can be computed (review finding 11): the compare-and-swap is a concurrency control, not a boundary against an attacker. A restore of the WAL and the ratchet together is not detected.
